unlisted_practices: Position the clinician as the content originator of a single core clinical narrative synthesis explaining what was thought and why, with AI rendering that intent into formats tailored to different stakeholders.
Do not rely on AI to write the clinical note's reasoning; design documentation technology to amplify rather than replace the clinician's voice.
Design EHR interfaces around the clinical narrative as the primary canvas, with structured data capture as a background assistant.
Allow layered documentation in which structured billing, quality, and secondary-use fields are captured or appended in parallel to the clinician's core narrative.
Reintegrate narrative competence and clinical reasoning documentation into clinician training, moving away from data-first presentations.
Document the differential diagnosis, including why competing diagnoses were discarded, and document contingency plans and pivot points in the assessment and plan.
Close the loop on findings raised in notes, such as documenting follow-up of suspicious imaging findings, and avoid copy-forward of outdated content.

screen.reason: Editorial discussing the risks of ambient AI and LLMs in clinical documentation, offering recommendations for clinical narrative preservation and governance.
